title: Kirby Problem 1.42
statement:
Do there exist algebraically concordant Seifert forms $V_{1}$ and
$V_{2}$ for which there do not exist concordant knots $K_{1}$ and $K_{2}$ with Seifert forms $V_{1}$
and $V_{2}$, respectively?
background:
Source: Kirby's Problems in Low-Dimensional Topology notes. Original problem number: KP-1.42.

Literature notes:
(1) Seifert forms $V_{1}$ and $V_{2}$ are algebraically concordant if $V_{1} \oplus -V_{2}$ is meta-
bolic. This problem is open regardless of whether one works with topo-
logical or smooth concordance of knots.

(2) As an example, the Seifert forms

$$
V_1=\begin{pmatrix}3&2\\1&3\end{pmatrix}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
V_2=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\1&9\end{pmatrix}
$$

are algebraically concordant: the set of vectors $\{(0, -3, 6, -1), (2, -1, 0, 1)\}$
is a basis for a metabolizer of $V_{1} \oplus -V_{2}$. Does there exist a pair of con-
cordant knots $K_{1}$ and $K_{2}$ having these Seifert forms? Conjecture 1.11
of [Liv01] posits that any knots $K_{1}$ and $K_{2}$ having as Seifert forms these
particular $V_{1}$ and $V_{2}$, respectively, cannot be concordant.

References cited:
- [Liv01] Charles Livingston. Examples in concordance, 2001. arXiv:math/0101035v1.
